extractor: read from the USCIS and CBP pages registered in source_roles, fetched from the VPS with the source monitor's own User-Agent
policy: Every entry quotes the official page it was read from, verbatim. This route previously held only travel.state.gov and ceac.state.gov sources, which refuse the monitor, so it published nothing.
structure_note: READ THE ASYMMETRY BEFORE READING THE REQUIREMENTS. The B classification has two halves and the Department of Homeland Security publishes only one of them: USCIS has a page for B-1 (business) and no equivalent page for B-2 (tourism), because B-2 involves no work and therefore falls outside what USCIS publishes under 'Working in the United States'. Every eligibility requirement below is a B-1 requirement and is labelled as such. What IS recorded for the whole classification is admission and extension — CBP inspects every arrival regardless of half, and the USCIS extension rules apply to both. The B-2 eligibility criteria are named in not_extracted rather than inferred from the B-1 list they resemble.
freshness_note: Both USCIS pages publish Last Reviewed/Updated dates in their markup; the CBP page does not and is reported as unknown.
not_extracted: The B-2 tourism eligibility criteria. No DHS host we can read publishes them, and they are NOT assumed to mirror the B-1 list on the same visa. The B-2 criteria are published by the Department of State, whose host returns HTTP 403 to the monitor. This is the largest gap on the route and it is stated rather than filled.
The visa application fee and the consular application procedure. Set and published by the Department of State.
Which nationalities need no visa. Deferred by USCIS to CBP and covered by the separate Visa Waiver Program route.
The Form I-539 filing fee. Named as a required filing; no amount published on either page.

requirements.label: B-1: be participating in business activities of a commercial or professional nature
requirements.source_excerpt: you may be eligible for a b-1 visa if you will be participating in business activities of a commercial or professional nature in the united states, including, but not limited to: consulting with business associates traveling for a scientific, educational, professional or business convention, or a conference on specific dates settling an estate negotiating a contract participating in short-term training
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You may be eligible for a B-1 visa if you will be participating in business activities of a commercial or professional nature in the United States, including, but not limited to: Consulting with business associates Traveling for a scientific, educational, professional or business convention, or a conference on specific dates Settling an estate Negotiating a contract Participating in short-term training

requirements.label: B-1: the purpose of your trip is business of a legitimate nature
requirements.source_excerpt: the purpose of your trip is to enter the united states for business of a legitimate nature
requirements.source_excerpt_display: The purpose of your trip is to enter the United States for business of a legitimate nature

requirements.label: Everyone arriving at a port of entry is inspected by CBP officers
requirements.description: Applies to both halves of the B classification and to every other status. The inspection has three components and CBP conducts all of them.
requirements.source_excerpt: all persons arriving at a port-of-entry to the united states are subject to inspection by cbp officers. cbp officers will conduct the immigration, customs, and agriculture components of the inspections process.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: All persons arriving at a port-of-entry to the United States are subject to inspection by CBP officers. CBP officers will conduct the Immigration, Customs, and Agriculture components of the Inspections process.

requirements.label: The Form I-94 admission record is the proof of legal visitor status
requirements.description: Recorded because the I-94 — not the visa — carries the date the stay actually expires, and that distinction decides who is out of status.
requirements.source_excerpt: international travelers visiting the united states can apply for a provisional i-94 or retrieve their i-94/i-95 admission number/record (which is proof of legal visitor status) as well as retrieve a limited travel history of their u.s. arrivals and departures.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: International travelers visiting the United States can apply for a provisional I-94 or retrieve their I-94/I-95 admission number/record (which is proof of legal visitor status) as well as retrieve a limited travel history of their U.S. arrivals and departures.

requirements.label: An immigration official must authorise your admission; the period granted may run up to one year
requirements.source_excerpt: at the port of entry, an immigration official must authorize your admission to the united states, and, if you are eligible for admission, you may be admitted initially for the period necessary to carry out your business activities, up to a maximum period of 1 year.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: At the port of entry, an immigration official must authorize your admission to the United States, and, if you are eligible for admission, you may be admitted initially for the period necessary to carry out your business activities, up to a maximum period of 1 year.

requirements.label: To extend your stay: lawful admission on a nonimmigrant visa, still-valid status, no disqualifying crimes, no violations, and a passport valid for the whole stay
requirements.source_excerpt: you were lawfully admitted into the united states with a nonimmigrant visa; your nonimmigrant visa status remains valid; you have not committed any crimes that make you ineligible for a visa; you have not violated the conditions of your admission; and your passport is valid and will remain valid for the duration of your stay.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You were lawfully admitted into the United States with a nonimmigrant visa; Your nonimmigrant visa status remains valid; You have not committed any crimes that make you ineligible for a visa; You have not violated the conditions of your admission; and Your passport is valid and will remain valid for the duration of your stay.

requirements.label: Your authorised stay expires on the date in the lower right of your Form I-94 — not the date on the visa
requirements.description: The authority states where to look. Overstaying carries a re-entry bar and removal, both named on the same page.
requirements.source_excerpt: if you remain in the united states longer than authorized, you may be barred from returning and/or you may be removed (deported) from the united states. check the date in the lower right-hand corner of your form i-94, arrival-departure record , to determine the date your authorized stay expires.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: If you remain in the United States longer than authorized, you may be barred from returning and/or you may be removed (deported) from the United States. Check the date in the lower right-hand corner of your Form I-94, Arrival-Departure Record, to determine the date your authorized stay expires.

requirements.label: USCIS recommends applying to extend at least 45 days before your authorised stay expires
requirements.description: The authority's own recommendation, not a deadline. Recorded as recommended so it can never render as a rule.
requirements.source_excerpt: we recommend that you apply to extend your stay at least 45 days before your authorized stay expires.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: We recommend that you apply to extend your stay at least 45 days before your authorized stay expires.

requirements.label: Extensions are filed on Form I-539 or Form I-129 depending on the classification
requirements.source_excerpt: a request for an extension of stay (eos) is generally filed on a petition for a nonimmigrant worker ( form i-129 ) or application to extend/change nonimmigrant status ( form i-539 ), depending upon the nonimmigrant classification the petitioner or applicant seeks to extend.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: A request for an extension of stay (EOS) is generally filed on a Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker (Form I-129) or Application to Extend/Change Nonimmigrant Status (Form I-539), depending upon the nonimmigrant classification the petitioner or applicant seeks to extend.

requirements.label: Six categories may not apply to extend at all — including Visa Waiver Program entrants and transit
requirements.description: A closed list, and the first entry catches most short-stay visitors: anyone admitted under the Visa Waiver Program cannot extend, whatever their circumstances.
requirements.source_excerpt: you may not apply to extend your stay if you were admitted to the united states in the following categories: visa waiver program; crew member (d nonimmigrant visa); in transit through the united states (c nonimmigrant visa); in transit through the united states without a visa (twov); fiancé(e) of a u.s. citizen or dependent of a fiancé(e) (k nonimmigrant visa); or informant (and accompanying family) on terrorism or organized crime (s nonimmigrant visa).
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You may not apply to extend your stay if you were admitted to the United States in the following categories: Visa Waiver Program; Crew member (D nonimmigrant visa); In transit through the United States (C nonimmigrant visa); In transit through the United States without a visa (TWOV); Fiancé(e) of a U.S. citizen or dependent of a fiancé(e) (K nonimmigrant visa); or Informant (and accompanying family) on terrorism or organized crime (S nonimmigrant visa).

requirements.label: There is no dependent visa — each family member applies separately for a B-2
requirements.source_excerpt: your spouse and children are not eligible for a dependent visa. each of your dependents who will be accompanying or following to join you must apply separately for a b-2 visa and must follow the regulations for that visa.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Your spouse and children are not eligible for a dependent visa. Each of your dependents who will be accompanying or following to join you must apply separately for a B-2 visa and must follow the regulations for that visa.
